title: Trump Concedes Iran War Helped Sink Republicans, Says He Would Do It Again
dek: After Democrats won control of Congress, Trump said the Iran war and gas prices were factors in the GOP losses, while defending the decision to strike Iran and dismissing impeachment talk.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Capitol, west front (file photo)

keyPoints: Trump told reporters the Iran war contributed to the midterm losses, saying it was 'largely true' according to CNN, and that surging gas prices from the 8-month-old conflict frustrated voters, the Associated Press reported.
Trump said he would make the same decision on Iran again and that it was worth it. Vice President JD Vance had written, 'The reason we lost is the war.'
Trump said he was not worried about a new impeachment effort 'not even a little bit.' CNN reported the House could vote as soon as next week to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
Trump told Politico he did not want to 'be just sitting there for two years vetoing everything,' and said he was not considering replacing Hegseth.
body:
President Donald Trump acknowledged on Wednesday that the Iran war and rising fuel prices were among the reasons Republicans lost control of Congress, while insisting the military campaign was the right choice.

## What Trump said

Trump told reporters the war had affected the midterm results, saying voters were frustrated by gas prices that rose during the eight-month conflict, according to the Associated Press. He told reporters the Iran war impact was 'largely true,' CNN reported, and said he agreed with Vance's assessment.

Trump also argued that public discontent was about 'the price, not the war,' and said the war had pushed gas prices up 'a little, short term,' according to Yahoo News' account of his remarks. Asked whether the war had been worth it, he answered yes. 'The Iran thing we had to do, and we continue to do it,' the AP quoted him saying.

## Impeachment and Hegseth

Trump said he was not worried about a possible new impeachment effort, which Democrats could pursue with their House majority. He said such a step would 'destroy' the Democratic Party, according to Yahoo News. He also said he was not considering replacing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and called him 'doing a great job,' the AP reported.

CNN reported that many Republican lawmakers and allies were moving to blame Hegseth for the losses, and that the House could vote as soon as next week on impeaching him. The reporting reviewed for this story does not establish how many votes such a measure would have.

## Democrats' response

AP reported that House Democrats plan to move quickly to reverse GOP cuts to the Affordable Care Act and Medicaid, and to begin a broad oversight agenda. Senate Democrats have sent document-preservation letters ahead of expected investigations, CNN reported.

## What is not yet known

Whether Congress will take up impeachment of Hegseth, and how Democrats will proceed on oversight, will depend on votes and the new Congress convening Jan. 3, 2027.
